| Check rules | Unit cycles while typing (`diagnostics.usesCycleLive`): rule `uses-cycle` in the editor with the shortest path at the triggering uses entry, an error when every edge lies in the interface (F2047); every unit in the hover jumps to its uses entry, “Show graph” opens the unit relations; quick fix “Move to implementation uses” (sorted with `sortUses`) when no identifier of the unit is needed in the interface section, otherwise jumps to those identifiers; also cycles with an implementation edge as a hint (`diagnostics.usesCycleImplementation`); off = no message in the editor, the project-wide check (#64) stays | on, off | atlas.json (Atlas › Project settings, page Check rules) | no | Checkbox, checkbox | #896 |
| Compiler | Builds for AI assistants (`compiler.mcpBuild`, quick toggle): the MCP tool `build_project` may build open projects in this IDE through IOTAProjectBuilder (make, build, check; configuration and platform only for this build) and receives the result and compiler messages, also in the Starter Edition without a command-line compiler. Refused with a reason while the debugger, another build or the compiler check is running; off = the IDE accepts no requests | on | Plugin (registry `McpBuild`) | no | Checkbox | #261 |
| Compiler | Run DUnitX tests (#69, `tests.run`, quick toggle): commands “Run tests” (*Atlas.RunTests*) and “Re-run failed tests” (*Atlas.RunFailedTests*) in the command palette; the test project is the active one or one of the project group whose main file uses `DUnitX.TestFramework` (for a single test the test project that contains its test unit); with several candidates Atlas asks once and remembers the choice for exactly these candidates (#585, locally in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Atlas\test-projects.json`); platform and configuration from the test project; result via the XML logger of DUnitX, failed tests as problems at the test method (source `DUnitX`, expected and actual value) and in the messages view; off = commands, code lens and the run after the build disappear | on | Plugin (registry `TestRun`) | no | Checkbox | #69 |
| Compiler | Build before the tests (`tests.buildFirst`): “Run tests” builds the test project first (make) like `build_project`; off = the existing test EXE runs without the compiler | on | Plugin (registry `TestsBuildFirst`) | no | Checkbox | #69 |
| Compiler | Tests after the build (`tests.afterBuild`, quick toggle): after every successful build of a DUnitX test project started by the user its tests run (compile events #527); not after the background check and not after builds for AI assistants | off | Plugin (registry `TestsAfterBuild`) | no | Checkbox | #69 |
| Compiler | Run affected tests (#1353, `tests.affected` in settings.json, quick toggle; depth `tests.affectedDepth`): command “Run affected tests” (*Atlas.RunAffectedTests*, Atlas menu and command palette) asks the server for the tests reached by the changes against the base (Git: merge base with main, SVN: BASE; including uncommitted changes) and runs only those like “Run tests”; if all are needed (project file changed, analysis incomplete), all run. Offer before the commit (`tests.affectedBeforeCommit`): Atlas installs a pre-commit hook in `.git/hooks` that names the affected tests and runs them in the terminal on request (Git only; Atlas leaves a foreign hook alone) | on, 3, off | settings.json (`tests.affected`, `tests.affectedDepth`), Plugin (registry `TestsAffectedBeforeCommit`) | no | Checkbox, number, checkbox | #1353 |

| Compiler | Check before the compile (`build.gate`: off, warn, block): before every make and build started by the user (not Code Insight, background check, syntax check or requests from AI assistants) Atlas checks the units changed since the last successful compile with the IDE buffers (also unsaved) for syntax errors and rule findings with severity error; the findings appear in the Atlas group of the messages window (double-click jumps there). off = no check, warn = report, block = cancel the compile; a second compile without changes within 10 s runs anyway (deliberate override). The same applies to the release build guard (#533), where off and warn only report | off | Plugin (registry `BuildGate`) | no | Choice | #529, #533 |
| Compiler | Time limit of the check before the compile (`build.gateTimeoutMs`, 50 to 10000 ms): if the check takes longer, the compile runs unchecked and Atlas reports this once per session | 300 | Plugin (registry `BuildGateTimeoutMs`) | no | Number | #529 |
| Compiler | Window “Compiler switches” (`build.compilerSwitches`, quick toggle): dockable window with the effective compiler switches at the cursor position: `R`, `Q`, `O`, `C`, `I`, `A`, `HINTS`, `WARNINGS`, warnings switched off or reported as errors (`{$WARN … OFF}`), active symbols as well as platform and configuration. For each value its origin: project option (property of the .dproj), compiler default, include file or directive with line (`R−, set in line 10`). Deviations from the .dproj are highlighted. Computed by the server through the preprocessor up to the cursor line (`atlas/compilerSwitches`), 150 ms after the last cursor movement. Double-click or Enter jumps to the directive or opens the project options. Command `Atlas.CompilerSwitches` | on | Plugin (registry `BuildCompilerSwitches`) | no | Checkbox | #558 |
| Compiler | Deviating compiler switches in the status bar (`build.showSwitchesInStatusBar`): extra panel in the editor status bar with the switches that deviate from the .dproj at the cursor position, such as `R− Q− HINTS OFF` or `WARN SYMBOL_PLATFORM OFF`; without a deviation no panel appears. The tooltip names the origin, a click opens the window “Compiler switches”. Only works with `build.compilerSwitches` | off | Plugin (registry `BuildSwitchesInStatusBar`) | no | Checkbox | #558 |
| Compiler | Start profiles (#575, `startProfiles.enabled`, quick toggle): command “Start profile: …” (*Atlas.StartProfile*, command palette) and a click on the status bar panel choose for the active project a profile from `startProfiles` of the project file `.atlas` (shared, needs `teamFile.enabled`) or a personal one; Atlas sets parameters, working folder, host application and environment variables of the active configuration and platform (like *Run › Parameters*), *Run* and *Run without debugging* then use them; the active profile applies per project and is set again when the project, configuration or platform changes; “No start profile” restores the run options from before the first profile; “Save current run options as personal profile …”; panel “Start profile: <name>” in the status bar as soon as the project has profiles (`startProfiles.statusField`, quick toggle); off = command, panel and tip disappear, the run options stay as they are | on, on | Plugin (registry `StartProfiles`, `StartProfilesStatusField`); personal profiles, active profile and the previous run options per project only locally in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Atlas\startprofiles\<key>.json`; shared ones in `.atlas` | no | Checkbox, checkbox | #575 |

| Release build | Release build guard (`build.releaseGuard`, quick toggle): before make and build in a release configuration Atlas checks the project options as the running IDE uses them for the build (with inherited values, also unsaved; not the .dproj on disk), according to `build.releaseChecks`. Violations appear in the Atlas group of the messages window with rule ID and a hint where to change the option. Also applies to builds through the runner (Claude Code `build_project`, “Open and build” #764), never to debug configurations, the background check, syntax check, clean or Code Insight. Command “Check release build” (*Atlas.CheckRelease*, command palette) checks the active project without a build. Result and version of every successful release build are stored in the section `release` of the project summary; off = no check and no command | on | Plugin (registry `ReleaseGuard`) | no | Checkbox | #533 |
| Release build | Release configurations (`build.releaseConfigs`, separated by commas; “Release” always applies, case does not matter) | Release | Plugin (registry `ReleaseConfigs`) | no | Text field | #533 |
| Release build | Checks of the guard (`build.releaseChecks`, separated by commas; `-name` switches one off): `debugDefine` (symbol DEBUG), `debugInfo` (debug information; with target value off also “Link with debug information”), `stackFrames`, `assertions`, `rangeChecks`, `overflowChecks` (each with target value `=off` or `=on`; if the option is missing, the compiler default applies), `memoryLeaks` (`ReportMemoryLeaksOnShutdown := True` in the project source outside `{$IFDEF DEBUG}`), `versionInfo` (no version information or the same version as in the last successful release build of the same configuration and platform; not with an auto-incremented build number), `outputFolder` (output folder equal to that of the Debug configuration). Packages without `memoryLeaks` and `outputFolder`. Rule IDs `release-debug-define` to `release-output-folder` | all on, target values off | Plugin (registry `ReleaseChecks`) | no | Checkbox or choice per check | #533 |
| Debugging | Debug a single test (#585, `tests.debug`, quick toggle): commands “Debug test at cursor” (*Atlas.DebugTest*) and “Run test at cursor” (*Atlas.RunTest*, with `tests.run`) in the command palette, entries “Debug test”/“Run test” in the editor context menu and the mark “Debug” of the code lens at `[TestFixture]`, `[Test]` and each `[TestCase]`; Atlas builds the test project (like “Run tests”), temporarily sets the run parameters `--run:<Unit.Fixture.Method[.Case]>` through the start profiles (#575) (existing parameters stay, `--run`, `--include`, `--exclude`, `--xmlfile` and `--exitbehavior` give way) and starts it in the debugger; afterwards the active project and run parameters are as before (also after a crash at the next start), the result appears as with “Run tests”. | Debugging | Variable values in the hover (`debug.hoverValues`, quick toggle): while the process is paused, Atlas evaluates the expression under the mouse (identifier with the qualifiers to its left, e.g. `FList.Count`; nothing in strings, comments and with calls) through the IDE debugger without side effects and shows the value at the top of the Atlas tooltip; if the debugger answers with a delay (Win64), it shows “evaluating …”; with the own tooltip off Atlas passes the value to the IDE tooltip | on | Plugin (registry `DebugHoverValues`) | no | Checkbox | #891 |
| Debugging | Explain “no access” while debugging (`debug.explainUnavailable`, quick toggle): if evaluating a value in the hover or in the values in the editor fails with a known IDE text (German and English, such as “Inaccessible value” or “… not … because of optimization”; own additions in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Atlas\debug-unavailable.txt`), it shows `‹no access›`. The hover names the cause in a fixed order: started in a configuration without debug information, `$D-`/`$L-` at the location, `$O+` (variable in a register), lifetime exceeded or not yet begun (approximation), routine `inline`, library frame without debug DCUs; plus the origin of the switch and fixes with preview: Restart with Debug, `{$OPTIMIZATION OFF}`/`ON` around the routine, `{$O-}` at the start of the unit, use debug DCUs, go to the directive. Without a match “Cause unknown” with the checked items | on | Plugin (registry `DebugExplainUnavailable`) | no | Checkbox | #840 |
| Debugging | Completion in debugger dialogs (`debug.completionInDialogs`, quick toggle): in “Evaluate/Modify” (Ctrl+F7), in the expression of a watch and in the condition and “Eval expression” of a breakpoint Atlas opens its own popup with identifiers from the scope: local variables, parameters, fields of `Self`, units and global names, after `.` the members. The scope is the execution point while the program is paused, its line in the breakpoint dialog, otherwise the cursor line in the editor. The list opens at the first letter of a word and after `.`, Ctrl+Space opens it by hand. Arrow down in the empty field shows the last 20 expressions of the project (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Atlas\debug-expressions.json`) | on | Plugin (registry `DebugCompletionInDialogs`) | no | Checkbox | #538 |
| Debugging | Window “Evaluate” (`debug.evaluateWindow`, quick toggle): dockable window “Atlas: Evaluate” (command `Atlas.DebugEvaluate`): Enter adds an expression, Del removes it; at every stop Atlas re-evaluates all rows in time slices and marks values that changed since the last stop. Objects, records and arrays expand, the fields come from the Atlas index (without the server from the result string) and are evaluated one by one. state field, user field, state on start and target states per connection in `issues.connections` (`stateField`, `assigneeField`, `startState`, `endStates`), otherwise the global values; drop-down lists “Load values from tracker”; track time per issue (`issues.timeTracking`, #1267, quick toggle, off = neither display nor file nor dialog): the clock runs while an issue is current and the IDE is active (input, debugger run), idle time beyond `issues.idleMinutes` stops it and is not counted; status panel “ATL-123 · 1:25” with pause/resume, reset, correct; storage per issue and day in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Atlas\time.json` (file lock, several IDEs do not count twice); on finishing or switching “… book?” with duration (rounded to `issues.timeRounding` minutes), work type and description, buttons Book, Later, Discard; YouTrack as a work item, GitHub optionally as a comment “Effort: …”; command *Pending time entries …*; checklists in the preview (`issues.preview.checklists`, #1273): task lists of the description (`- [ ]`, `* [x]`, `1. [ ]`, also indented, not in code blocks) as ticks with “3/5” in the header; ticking loads the current description, checks the line (text and position), changes only `[ ]`/`[x]` and writes back (YouTrack `POST /api/issues/<key>`, GitHub `PATCH …/issues/<n>`); if it has changed in the meantime, Atlas writes nothing and reloads; “Add item …” appends `- [ ] text`; without write permission read-only, checklists in comments read-only; off = list as text; progress of the current issue in the status panel (`issues.checklistStatus`, row `atlas.issue.checklist` “ATL-131 · 3/5”, a click opens the preview at the list, without a checklist no row); links as a tree (`issues.preview.links`, #1279): depends on, blocks, subtasks with progress (2/3), parent, duplicates, “relates to” and mentions collapsed, per row icon (open, done, blocked), key, title and state, plus “Create subtask …” and “Link …” (YouTrack and GitHub; off: flat list); warning on “Start” as long as a “depends on” issue is open (`issues.warnBlocked`); board (`issues.board`, #1272, *Atlas.Board*, View › Atlas › Board): dock window “Atlas board” with the columns of the agile board (YouTrack, board and sprint selectable, “current sprint” preselected) or of the GitHub project (status field, iterations as sprints; without a project or without the permission `read:project` Open/Closed with a note), cards with key, title, initials of the assignee, priority stripe, checklist progress and lock; “Mine only”/“All” (`issues.board.onlyMine` = filter on opening), search, refresh; dragging into another column asks (`issues.board.confirmMove`, “Don't ask again” switches it off) with an optional comment and writes via the same ways as “Finish” (YouTrack `POST /api/commands`, GitHub `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue` or closing/reopening), on error the card jumps back; double-click opens the preview, context menu Start, Open in browser, Assign to me; the current issue is highlighted; narrow (below 360 pixels) as a list grouped by columns; last state in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Atlas\issues\<tracker>-board.json`, offline with a note; sprint tile (#1277): burndown with actual line, dashed ideal line, mark “today” and tooltip per day (`issues.sprint.burndown`), comparison with the previous sprint (pale line normalized to sprint days, “done 5 · previous sprint 4 on the same day ▲1”) and velocity of the last three sprints as bars (`issues.sprint.compare`; off = no earlier sprint is queried; finished sprints queried once and cached as `<tracker>-sprint-<board>-<sprint>.json`); search issues in the command palette (`issues.paletteSearch`, #1270): `#text` or `ATL-text` searches in the tracker, `#42` or `ATL-12` reads the issue directly, an empty `#` shows the recently opened ones without a network query; Enter preview, Ctrl+Enter Start, Shift+Enter browser, Ctrl+C copy key; comment editor (`issues.commentEditor`, #1278) in the preview and in the finish dialog: “@” suggests users of the tracker (YouTrack login and name, GitHub assignable users), “#” or `ATL-` issues; arrows, Enter or Tab, Esc; Ctrl+B bold, Ctrl+I italic, Ctrl+Shift+K code block, “Preview” with the renderer of the issue preview; drafts per tracker, issue and field in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Atlas\issues\drafts.json` (2 s after the last change and on closing, deleted after sending); off = plain text field; table “Snippets” (`issues.commentSnippets`, name and text with `{issue}`, `{branch}`, `{commit}`, `{version}`), inserted with Ctrl+Space or “Snippet ▾”; unchanged defaults follow the language of the IDE (#1458); tab “Development” with branches and commits for the key, pull requests with CI traffic light or linked changes and changed units, searched only when the tab is opened (`issues.preview.development`); messages about my issues (`issues.notify`, #1271, quick toggle): every connection (tracker of the `.atlas` and `issues.connections`) is asked for changes in the background (YouTrack: changed issues and their activities, GitHub: `/notifications` conditionally with If-Modified-Since), new comments by others, assignments and state changes appear combined per issue in the notification center (source “Issues”, pop up, only collect or off like other sources), “Open” shows the issue in “Atlas issue” at the first new comment, affected issues carry a dot in “My issues” until they were opened; Atlas does not report own changes, on first switching on “now” applies; only with an active IDE (minimized or 30 min without input pauses, caught up once afterwards), additionally when “My issues” is opened; an error (token refused, unreachable) comes once and not again until the next success; interval (`issues.notify.intervalMinutes`, 2–1440; doubled after errors up to 60 minutes, GitHub at least X-Poll-Interval), scope (`issues.notify.scope`: assigned, assignedOrCreated, watched); values of secret names as ***) and exception history in one step; the dialog shows names and sizes, sending happens only with “Send”; YouTrack uploads the files (`POST /api/issues/<key>/attachments`) and on request writes a comment with references, GitHub gets texts as a code block in the comment, pictures are on the clipboard (note “Paste in GitHub with Ctrl+V”) and the browser opens the issue; files stay in `%TEMP%\Atlas\attach` only until sending or cancelling; log files to suggest (`issues.attach.logFiles`, separated by “;”, with `$(ProjectDir)`, `$(ProjectName)`, environment variables and `*`), pictures at most this wide (`issues.attach.maxImageWidth`, 320–7680) | empty, branch, empty, empty, `{kennung} `, on, none, none, none, on, on, on, on, on, on, on, 200, on, on, State, Assignee, empty, off, empty, empty, `Done in {branch}.\n{commits}` (German IDE: `Erledigt in {branch}.\n{commits}`), off, 10, 5, on, on, on, on, on, on, on, on, on, on, on, two snippets (English IDE: “Please check with the current build”, “Fixed in {commit}”; ## Areas for export, import and reset

*Tools › Options › Atlas* and the command palette export, import and reset settings per area (#723, can be switched off with `settings.exportImport`). The area is determined by `x-area` in the schema: per plugin setting in the catalog `schemas/atlas-plugin.schema.json`, per global key in `atlas.schema.json`. New settings are thereby included without a further list. The export file `atlas-settings.json` contains only changed values, no credentials (`settings.exportSecrets`: omit or placeholder) and no paths with user names (user folders become `$(APPDATA)`, `$(LOCALAPPDATA)`, `$(USERPROFILE)`). Project and team values (`atlas.json`, `.atlas`) are neither exported nor overwritten on import.

## Experimental features

Risky or immature features come as **experimental** (#834): they have their own switch, are marked “Experimental” on the options page and in the quick switches (#604) and are off after installation. The master switch `experimental.enabled` (*Tools › Options › Atlas › General*, quick toggle “Allow experimental features”, default off) releases them: while it is off, no experimental feature works, even if its switch is on; the switches keep their value. The profile “Everything on” (#723) does not switch them on; for that there is “Everything on, including experimental”. Status panel (tooltip), bug report and diagnostic log name the effective experimental switches (keys only). When a feature becomes stable, `x-experimental` is dropped; a stored value stays.

| Key | Place | Page | Origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `editor.multiCursor` | Plugin (registry `MultiCursor`) | Editor | #589 |
| `editor.linkedEditing` | Plugin (registry `LinkedEditing`) | Editor | #658 |
| `editor.smartPaste` | Plugin (registry `SmartPaste`) | Editor | #515 |
| `editor.designerBar.tabOrderClick` | Plugin (registry `DesignerTabOrderClick`) | Editor | #1442 |
| `editor.designerBar.align` | Plugin (registry `DesignerAlign`) | Editor | #1442 |
| `editor.minimap` | Plugin (registry `Minimap`) | Editor | #873 |
| `completion.typeConversion` | global (settings.json) | Completion | #490 |
| `completion.assignAllFields` | global (settings.json) | Completion | #491 |
| `refactoring.inline` | project (atlas.json) | Completion | #103 |
| `refactoring.moveClass` | project (atlas.json) | Completion | #103 |
| `refactoring.unitRenameFollowUp` | project (atlas.json) | Completion | #512 |

## Options page: sub-items and master switches

*Tools › Options › Atlas* shows a tree on the left (#890): the areas at the top, below them the sub-items per feature. The main node of an area carries its general options and an overview of all master switches of its sub-items (with “Details”). Every feature with a master switch has its own frame, the switch at the top, the sub-options indented below. While a master switch is off, all controls of its group are disabled (also nested groups); the values are kept and saved as well. Experimental features including their master switch are disabled as long as `experimental.enabled` is off. The master switch is determined by `x-parent` in the plugin catalog, otherwise by the prefix rule (longest prefix `P` with a Boolean setting `P` or `P.enabled`); the sub-item by `x-node` (IDs in `x-nodes`), otherwise the sub-item of the master switch. Structured by page (`x-page`) and sub-item; indented = sub-option of the switch above.
